> Operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are not executed when building the vignette because they require the project data.

# From routing metadata to a graph

`build_DAG()` reads routing metadata and produces the canonical DAG.
`stop_on_cycle = TRUE` prevents processing from continuing with cyclic
dependencies; `analyze = TRUE` computes structural diagnostics. The project
script also saves the adjacency matrix, transposed incidence matrix, numeric
routing table and graph partitions.

```{r build-dag}
source(file.path("scripts", "00_config.R"))
dag <- SSPICE::build_DAG(
  routing = config$routing_file,
  separator = config$metadata_separator,
  na_strings = config$missing_codes,
  analyze = TRUE,
  stop_on_cycle = TRUE,
  max_paths_per_partition = config$max_paths_per_partition
)
names(dag)
dag$graph_diagnostics
```

# What to inspect

Nodes represent variables and logical groups; edges represent path
prerequisites. Inspect sources, isolated nodes, partitions and path lengths
before attributing routing anomalies to the data. OR and XOR groups are
represented by canonical VOR and VXOR variables. An acyclic graph allows
dependencies to be evaluated in a consistent order.

```{r inspect-dag}
source(file.path("scripts", "01_build_DAG.R"))
dag <- readRDS(file.path(config$dag_output_dir, "questionnaire_DAG.rds"))
str(dag$graph_diagnostics, max.level = 1)
utils::head(dag$routes_numeric)
```

If construction fails, correct the metadata and rebuild the DAG before reusing
derived results. The DAG extended with logical edits is built separately in
Step 09.

# Checking the meaning of the graph

Read [Building the routing file](routing-02b.html) before constructing the
graph. Canonical nodes can replace several original variables: VOR and VXOR
are not simple renamings. In particular, check that jump targets still exist
after grouping.

An acyclic DAG can still contain incorrectly specified domains, jumps or
groups. Inspect `routes_original`, `routes_grouped`, `routes_numeric` and `Bt`,
and check expected paths on small examples. An isolated node may indicate a
question excluded by an unconditional jump or a metadata error; do not remove
it automatically without interpreting its role.
